headline: India: Over 50 killed as Houthis target Yemen military camp with ballistic missiles
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- India: Over 50 killed as Houthis target Yemen military camp with ballistic missiles.
- Persian Gulf Region: US, Israel weigh renewed strikes on Iran as experts warn renewed conflict may be inevitable.
- South Asia: UN agency to end monthly aid to 500,000 people in Gaza over funding shortfall.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army acquisition command awards contracts worth $6.8B in 2026.
- Military Times, 11 hours ago: US Army acquisition command awards contracts worth $6.8B in 2026.
The Mission and Installation Contracting Command awarded 21,450 contracts in fiscal 2026 valued at $6.8 billion in total, a boost from the year prior.
- Military Times, 12 hours ago: US Army showing interest in G/ATOR missile-killing radar, Northrop says.
Northrop Grumman’s new multi-mission radar system has earned high marks from Marine Corps leadership. The U.S. Army has taken notice.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Miss KSA Festival Queen launches ‘The Refinery’ for teen moms.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: Miss KSA Festival Queen launches ‘The Refinery’ for teen moms.
Miss Kingston and St Andrew (KSA) Festival Queen Danielle Cox has officially launched her parish project, aimed at addressing the lack of empowerment and access to resources for teenage mothers in her home region. The project, dubbed ‘The Refinery: Becoming, Not Broken’, began in March 2026 at the Mary’s Child Home. According to Cox, who was the second runner-up in the National Festival Queen Coronation in August, not enough is being done to make young mothers aware of opportunities that exits for them.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: Ralph, Stewart celebrated for global achievements, commitment to Ja.
MANHATTAN, New York: One conquered Hollywood and Broadway, becoming an Emmy Award-winning actress and humanitarian. The other helped transform a Jamaican hotel company into one of the Caribbean’s most internationally recognised hospitality brands. Last Friday night, their journeys converged at The Plaza in Manhattan, New York, where Sheryl Lee Ralph and Adam Stewart were celebrated at the American Friends of Jamaica’s (AFJ) 45th anniversary Hummingbird Gala for achievements that have carried Jamaica’s influence far beyond its shores.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Ambulance driver killed in Russian attack on Kherson while his crew was rescuing injured civilians.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Ambulance driver killed in Russian attack on Kherson while his crew was rescuing injured civilians.
Serhii Honcharov, an emergency medical technician, was killed in a Russian airstrike on Kherson on 17 October while saving injured civilians.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Russian attack on park in Kharkiv Oblast: six killed, including two children – photos.
The attack on Nova Vodolaha’s central park injured 15 people, including seven children. A café building was damaged, and investigators have opened a war crimes case after the strike on the crowded park.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Commander of 3rd Army Corps explains why Lyman offensive was named Vivaldi.
Andrii Biletskyi, Commander of the 3rd Army Corps, has said that the offensive operation near Lyman was named Vivaldi because it was initially planned to have four stages. The idea came from two officers in the corps, one of whom was killed and the other seriously wounded.
- The Moscow Times, 8 hours ago: Annexed Crimea Begins Lifting Fuel Rationing Measures After Months of Shortages.
Crimea began rationing fuel in May after Ukrainian drone strikes targeted military trucks and fuel tankers that supply the region from the north.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Trump says he is open to trilateral summit with Putin and Xi.
- Politico Europe, Dawn (Pakistan), NDTV - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, The Moscow Times, The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: Trump says he is open to trilateral summit with Putin and Xi.
The president told reporters that such a meeting would focus on denuclearization, not the war in Ukraine as Moscow had suggested earlier.
- Balkan Insight, 7 hours ago: Serbians Linked to Protest Movement Allegedly Hit by Spyware Attacks.
Six days before crucial Serbian parliamentary elections, digital rights investigators report with “high confidence” that two prominent figures connected to the anti-government protest movement were targeted by spyware.
- Politico Europe, 13 hours ago: Serbian prosecutor probing Trump Tower in Belgrade targeted with spyware.
The revelations come amid mounting controversy over plans to redevelop the former Yugoslav military headquarters in Belgrade into a new luxury Trump Tower.
- Balkan Insight, 17 hours ago: Ukraine’s EU Accession Push Is Gaining Momentum, Says Ambassador to Moldova.
Paun Rohovei tells BIRN that Ukraine is advancing EU-backed anti-corruption reforms and seeking closer security ties with Moldova and Romania. He also warns that a growing water crisis on the Dniester River threatens Moldova and Ukraine.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: US, Israel weigh renewed strikes on Iran as experts warn renewed conflict may be inevitable.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: US, Israel weigh renewed strikes on Iran as experts warn renewed conflict may be inevitable.
A possible US military campaign against Iran could target missile facilities and nuclear infrastructure, but experts caution that even a brief operation risks triggering a prolonged conflict.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: 160 people reported killed in escalating drone attacks across Sudan.
Rights groups warn increasing attacks by unmanned aircraft are targeting civilians and infrastructure.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: One killed in US shooting near mosque in Columbus, Ohio.
Local authorities say mosque was not target of attack.
- Jerusalem Post, 3 hours ago: Syria fears imminent Israeli-backed Druze offensive in Sweida, official tells 'Post'.
Damascus is increasingly concerned about a potential Druze offensive in Sweida, claiming Israel is encouraging armed groups and providing military support, a senior Syrian official told the Post.
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Drone Strikes Kill Civilians in Darfur and Kordofan As Attacks Target Eastern Sudan.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: Sudan: Drone Strikes Kill Civilians in Darfur and Kordofan As Attacks Target Eastern Sudan.
[Dabanga] Bir Saliba / Abu Zabad Locality / El Mazroub / Wad -- Drone attacks killed civilians in West Darfur and West Kordofan on Saturday, including women, while further strikes targeted military installations in eastern Sudan. A separate fire destroyed up to 80 commercial stalls in Northern State.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 13 hours ago: Mali: Malian Army and Rebels Committing Abuses Against Civilians, Rights Group Says.
[RFI] The Malian army and its Russian paramilitary allies have killed civilians in violation of international law, Human Rights Watch (HRW) has said in a new report, which also confirms the al-Qaeda-linked jihadist group (JNIM) summarily executed Malian soldiers following an attack on a military convoy in July.
- Africanews, 17 hours ago: DR Congo: Ebola outbreak deepens mental health crisis amid stigma and conflict.
The World Health Organization has warned that it could surpass the deadliest Ebola outbreak in history, which erupted more than a decade ago and killed more than 11,000 people in West Africa.
- Africanews, 15 hours ago: Mali's army and rebel opponents guilty of human rights violations, new report finds.
Mali's army and its Russian paramilitary allies have killed civilians in violation of international law, according to a new report from Human Rights Watch. The army's rebel opponents have done the same, the report claims.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: Paychangu Lands Reserve Bank of Malawi Licence to Expand Digital Payments.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 13 hours ago: Malawi: Paychangu Lands Reserve Bank of Malawi Licence to Expand Digital Payments.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi's push towards a more digitised economy received a boost after the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) granted PayChangu a Payment Service Provider (PSP) licence, allowing the locally owned fintech group to offer payment aggregation services nationwide.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 13 hours ago: Malawi: Malawi to Roast in 42c Heatwave As Experts Warn Lives Could Be At Risk.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi is set to swelter under a brutal heatwave this week, with temperatures predicted to soar to a scorching 42C in some areas, prompting urgent health warnings from authorities.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 13 hours ago: Malawi: Bible Warning for Mutharika Critics - Mwanamvekha Warns DPP Against Divisions.
[Nyasa Times] Finance Minister Joseph Mwanamvekha has delivered a blunt warning to Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) members, telling ambitious figures to stop tearing each other down in the race for power and instead focus on helping President Peter Mutharika rebuild Malawi.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 17 hours ago: Zimbabwe: 'Failure to Toe Zanu-PF Party Line Has Consequences' - Mnangagwa Warns Dissenters.
[New Zimbabwe] PRESIDENT Emmerson Mnangagwa has downplayed a glaring rift with his deputy, Vice President Constantino Chiwenga, describing it as normal in a revolutionary party like ZANU PF, but warned that those who fail to toe the party line will fall by the wayside.

ASIA
India - bottom line: Over 50 killed as Houthis target Yemen military camp with ballistic missiles.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 12 hours ago: Over 50 killed as Houthis target Yemen military camp with ballistic missiles.
A deadly Houthi missile attack on a military training camp in Shabwa province killed at least 50 coalition fighters. The attack also resulted in over two dozen troops wounded, according to military officials. Following the strikes, Yemeni forces reported recapturing territory in Taiz governorate, while Houthi forces continued their offensive. In another incident, a coalition airstrike killed nine people, including children and women, in Saada.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: 6 ops in 48 hrs: Houthis claim to strike Saudi airports, oil field & military sites.
Yemen's Iran-linked Houthi rebels announced six military operations targeting Saudi Arabia over the last 48 hours. They claimed to have struck strategic sites including oil facilities and airports, causing significant damage and disruption. This escalation followed reported Saudi airstrikes on Yemeni civilian areas, resulting in numerous casualties. Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree highlighted the Houthis' use of ballistic missiles and drones in these operations.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Russian Strikes In Ukraine's Kharkiv Kill Infant In Stroller, 5 Others.
Kharkiv regional governor Oleg Synegubov said on Telegram that the dead in the attack in Nova Vodolaga included three children and that 14 others were wounded.
- NDTV - Top Stories, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Video: In "World's First", Ukraine Airlifts Injured Soldier With Drone.
The brigade published a video showing the drone lowering itself to the ground, before a man in combat gear fastens himself to a winch onboard and is lifted upwards.
South Asia - bottom line: UN agency to end monthly aid to 500,000 people in Gaza over funding shortfall.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: UN agency to end monthly aid to 500,000 people in Gaza over funding shortfall.
The World Food Programme said Monday it would end monthly assistance to 500,000 people in Gaza due to a funding shortfall, despite acute needs in the war-battered Palestinian territory. With the cutbacks, 1.1 million Palestinians in Gaza — still about half the population — will be receiving either food or cash assistance each month from the UN agency, in reduced amounts. The World Food Programme (WFP) said its efforts had mitigated the effects during a famine last year in Gaza and warned that conditions had not improved to the point that it can take away aid. “People are not safe.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: 'We never gave up': Naqvi highlights Pakistan's peace efforts in US-Iran war at Qatar forum.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday highlighted Pakistan’s mediation efforts between the United States and Iran, affirming that Islamabad “never gave up”. He made the remarks while addressing the 8th Global Security Forum being held in Qatar’s capital, Doha. Convened under the title “The Future of Alliances“, the forum brings together high-ranking officials and dignitaries from over 100 nations, according to Qatar News Agency. “The last few months have been very difficult for our region.

“Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv region and more than 200 drones across the war-torn country,” Volodymyr Zelenskyy said
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Army major martyred, 4 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR.
An army major was martyred and four terrorists were killed during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan, the military’s media wing said on Monday. The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement that security forces conducted a series of operations in areas of Shadi Kaur and Pasni in Gwadar, and Jattakabad in Kalat district, on the reported presence of multiple hideouts of Fitna al Hindustan. The state has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

The targets include Shanghai Zhisuan Technology, founded by former Google software engineer Ding Linwei, venture capital firm MiraclePlus and three related entities. It is not yet known whether the incidents were connected to each other. “Police investigating the circumstances of threatening emails sent to schools across Northern Ireland this morning … are treating the matter as a hoax,” authorities said.
